direct_answer: SBM Offshore integrates sustainability-related performance into the Management Board’s remuneration via its Short-Term Incentive (STI) program, which is based on key performance indicators across three performance indicator sets: profitability, growth and sustainability [Source 1][Source 3]. Climate/emission-related targets are explicitly included as part of the short-term incentive for the Management Board (and employees) [Source 6]. Target achievement for each performance measure in the Management Board remuneration policy is determined by the Supervisory Board, upon recommendation of the Appointment and Remuneration Committee [Source 1]. For the Supervisory Board itself, SBM Offshore states there are no performance targets (and no share-based incentives), to allow focus on long-term value creation [Source 1][Source 11].
compliance_rationale: The passages evidence that sustainability (including emission-related targets) is a performance area within the Management Board STI and that the Supervisory Board (on ARC recommendation) determines target achievement, and that the Supervisory Board has no performance targets [Source 1][Source 3][Source 6][Source 11]. However, the retrieved text does not provide the specific sustainability targets/impacts used, the proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability targets/impacts, nor the approval/update level for the incentive scheme terms beyond target achievement determination [Source 1][Source 3][Source 6].
disclosure_gaps: Specific sustainability-related targets and/or impacts used to assess performance (beyond the general reference to sustainability and emission-related targets) [Source 3][Source 6].

Explanation of how sustainability-related performance metrics are used as benchmarks or embedded in remuneration policies (beyond stating sustainability is a performance area and emission-related targets represent STI) [Source 1][Source 6].
Proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability-related targets/impacts (explicit percentage/weighting of sustainability within variable pay) [Source 1].

Level in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated (the evidence covers who determines target achievement, but not approval/update of scheme terms) [Source 1].
Key characteristics of the sustainability component of the incentive scheme (e.g., time horizon, measurement methodology, threshold/maximum mechanics for sustainability KPIs) [Source 3][Source 6].
key_findings: Management Board remuneration includes an STI based on KPIs, with sustainability performance as one of the performance areas [Source 1].
The Management Board STI uses three sets of performance indicators: profitability, growth and sustainability [Source 3].
Emission-related targets are included in the short-term incentive for the Management Board (and employees) [Source 6].
The Supervisory Board determines target achievement for each performance measure, upon recommendation of the Appointment and Remuneration Committee [Source 1].
The Supervisory Board has no performance targets and no share-based incentives [Source 1][Source 11].
